summary: Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport (HAH) is the primary international gateway to the Union of the Comoros, serving the capital city of Moroni on the island of Grande Comore. Named after a Comorian prince who served as President of the Government Council of the Comoros, the airport handles the majority of the archipelago's international flights. Its coastal location near the Indian Ocean provides a distinctive approach for arriving aircraft.
faqs:
Q: What is the main airport in Comoros?
A: Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport (HAH) in Moroni is the largest and busiest airport in Comoros, handling nearly all international traffic to the archipelago.

Q: Which airlines fly to Moroni airport?
A: The airport is served by regional carriers including Air Austral, Kenya Airways, and Comoros Aviation, with connections to destinations like Nairobi, Dzaoudzi, Antananarivo, and Réunion.

Q: How far is the airport from Moroni city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 15-20 km north of Moroni, with travel times of around 20-30 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Does the airport have international departures facilities?
A: Yes, the terminal handles international flights with standard customs and immigration services, though facilities are modest compared to larger regional hubs.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared minivans (taxis-brousse) are available outside the terminal for transfers to Moroni; agree on a price before departure as meters are not commonly used. Many hotels offer airport pickup services that can be arranged in advance. Car rentals are available but roads around Moroni can be narrow and winding, so a 4x4 is recommended for exploring beyond the city.
local_tip: Pack light and keep valuables in your carry-on, as checked baggage handling at this regional airport can be unpredictable—many experienced travelers recommend keeping essentials and a change of clothes in hand luggage.
